schema_note: One record per feature: idx, label, domain_class, evidence_tier, maxActApprox, density, sae_id, layer, width, l0_variant, low_confidence, plus documented extensions beyond gemma3_sweep's schema (density_ratio_to_population_median, mean_activation_when_firing, n_firings, matched_control_feature and related fields). Open schema, same convention as Gemma's manifest. Tier 1 (3 features) listed before tier 2 (9 features) -- see evidence_tier_note.
maxActApprox_caveat: maxActApprox here is Qwen's own max_activation, measured over the same 5,000-document / 1,712,777-token-position FineWeb stream for both tiers (scripts/characterize_lite.py) -- NOT comparable to Gemma's maxActApprox: different SAE architectures (topk vs JumpReLU), different training corpora and token counts, different activation scales entirely (Qwen ~10-60 typical vs Gemma's ~2000-10000+). Never compare these two columns' maxActApprox numbers directly.
sae_repo_id_caveat: Locally trained checkpoint, never published to a HF hub repo -- unlike Gemma's sae_repo_id, this is genuinely None, not an omission.
control_mechanism_note: Single global random draw via gemma3_sweep.pick_control_feature_idx (same mechanism as Gemma), excluded against ALL 12 features across both tiers plus every recorded reject and verified-but-not-selected idx -- not characterize_lite's own per-feature matched_control_feature, which is display-only metadata.
evidence_tier_note: Two evidence tiers, established by different methods, listed tier-1-first so a consumer (e.g. a UI dropdown) opens on the concept-validated demo rather than the taxonomy draw. Do not average or otherwise merge them into one population -- see each tier's own provenance fields (evidence_tier, plus job/procedure notes) for what differs.
labels_auto_derived_caveat: Tier-2 labels in this manifest are auto-derived by reading top_examples for a consistent trailing token/phrase pattern and are NOT human-adjudicated, unlike tier-1's (concept-validated) and Gemma's 9 (which went through the project's full adjudication process).
causal_screening_caveat: None of these 12 features have been causally screened. Gemma's 9 went through a 1736-record steer/ablate sweep and a 288-record necessity run; these features have had neither, and will not get either this week.
density_cross_sae_caveat: Absolute density (firing_rate) is not comparable across these two SAEs. Qwen's SAE is 163840-wide vs Gemma's 16384-wide (10x) -- a Qwen feature firing at the same rate as a Gemma feature corresponds to a much smaller share of the width-163840 feature budget firing at all, for reasons of SAE width, not model behavior. 'Qwen's features are rarer' would be a false reading of the raw density numbers alone.
density_band_disclosure: Gemma's 9 features span firing_rate/density [0.000782, 0.021364]. Exactly 8 of Qwen's 64 tier-2-pool features fall inside that exact band by firing_rate alone: 89549, 65931, 33008, 105490, 20990, 107244, 59622, 45344. One of those eight (65931) failed snippet verification and was rejected (see rejected_features). The tier-2 primary 9 therefore comprises 7 in-band survivors plus 2 features below Gemma's floor (37230 at 0.000716, 134801 at 0.000673) promoted from further down the firing_rate ranking to fill the two open slots. This is not the '8 in-band, 1 below floor' split a first pass anticipated -- it is 7 and 2 -- because verification, not the density band alone, is the real gate. Tier 1's own three features (2.3e-04 to 5.9e-04) are all below this band entirely -- see RANKING_NEAR_MISS_CAVEAT.
domain_class_spread_disclosure: Gemma's 9 span 6 domain classes: instruction(1), entity(4), temporal(1), abstract(1), numeric(1), syntax(1). Tier 2's primary 9 span only 3: syntax(5: 89549, 105490, 20990, 107244, 45344), entity(3: 59622, 37230, 134801), numeric(1: 33008). Zero instruction, temporal, or abstract features survive in the top-9-by-firing-rate ranking. Tier 2's optional 10th (145471) adds 'abstract'. Tier 1 adds 'topic' (all 3). Per instruction, this gap is disclosed rather than filled by reaching further down the ranking to manufacture spread.
tiebreaker_departure_note: Departure from Gemma's procedure, tier 2 only: Gemma's selection had no tiebreaker beyond the density band and snippet verification. This selection adds one -- among candidates that already passed snippet verification, prefer higher mean_activation_when_firing -- but it was not decisive for any of the 10 tier-2 slots filled here (no two verified candidates were close enough in firing-rate rank to need it); recorded because the rule exists and could bind on a future re-selection, not because it changed this one. Feature 105490's mean_activation_when_firing (13.836) is notably high against a ~5 typical among the other 9 candidates -- consistent with the tiebreaker's intent even though it wasn't invoked.
ranking_near_miss_caveat: Sixth caveat. The tier-2 selection criterion (rank by firing_rate descending) would have EXCLUDED all three tier-1 features had it been applied to the same 64-feature pool tier-1 was drawn from -- they fire at 2.3e-04 to 5.9e-04, below tier-2's own primary-9 floor (134801 at 6.7e-04). Recorded because the near-miss is informative about what density ranking actually selects for at this SAE width (163840-wide: the highest-firing features skew heavily syntactic/positional -- 5 of tier-2's 9 are domain_class=syntax -- not conceptual), not because tier 1 was at risk of being dropped from this manifest.
